manifest.title: Delivery Reliability & Bottleneck Analysis
manifest.description: An operations dashboard identifying where late-delivery risk and customer impact are concentrated across sellers, routes, regions, and product categories.

cards.description: Unique orders after normalizing the item-level source to order grain.
Share delivered after the estimated delivery timestamp.
Delay duration among late orders only.
Late-order average rating minus on-time average rating; association, not causation.

charts.title: Monthly late-delivery rate
charts.subtitle: 2018-03 peaked at 21.1%; the full-period network rate was 8.0%.
charts.question: When did delivery reliability deteriorate?
charts.rationale: A monthly line exposes sustained movement and operational spikes across 20 complete-volume periods.

charts.title: Late-delivery rate by purchase-to-carrier time
charts.subtitle: Orders handed to the carrier after seven days were 4.6x as likely to arrive late as orders handed off within two days.
charts.question: Does slow carrier handoff identify higher delivery risk?
charts.rationale: Ordered bars make the monotonic risk gradient easy to compare without implying causality.

charts.title: Low-review rate by delivery status
charts.subtitle: Low reviews occurred on 54.0% of late orders versus 9.1% of on-time orders.
charts.question: How strongly is lateness associated with poor customer ratings?
charts.rationale: A two-category bar shows the observed satisfaction gap while retaining denominators in the tooltip.

charts.title: Excess late orders by high-volume seller
charts.subtitle: Seller 06A2C3 recorded about 56 more late orders than expected at the network rate.
charts.question: Which high-volume sellers contribute the largest volume-adjusted delivery gap?
charts.rationale: Excess late orders balances seller volume and reliability while excluding ambiguous multi-seller orders.

charts.title: Excess late orders by seller-to-customer route
charts.subtitle: SP to RJ had the largest volume-adjusted route gap at about 587 excess late orders.
charts.question: Which state-to-state routes concentrate delivery underperformance?
charts.rationale: Route-level excess volume identifies operational lanes where seller origin and customer destination overlap with poor reliability.

charts.title: Excess late orders by customer state
charts.subtitle: RJ contributed about 640 more late orders than expected at the network rate.
charts.question: Where does delivery underperformance create the largest recoverable volume?
charts.rationale: Volume-adjusted excess late orders avoids prioritizing tiny states solely because of volatile rates.

charts.title: Excess late orders by product category
charts.subtitle: Health Beauty had the largest volume-adjusted excess among categories with at least 500 orders.
charts.question: Which large product categories warrant the first operational audit?
charts.rationale: Excess volume balances exposure and rate instead of ranking categories by rate alone.

query.description: Reviewed dashboard extract produced from an order-grain normalization of the cleaned Olist item-level parquet.
filters: One row per complete order
metric_definitions: Late-delivery rate = orders with delivery_delay_hours > 0 / analyzed orders
Material late rate = orders with delivery_delay_hours > 24 / analyzed orders
Low-review rate = review-eligible orders with review_score <= 2 / review-eligible orders
Excess late orders = observed late orders - (orders x network late-delivery rate)
Purchase-to-carrier time = time_to_ship_hours / 24
Seller metrics use complete single-seller orders so one final delivery outcome is not assigned to multiple sellers
High-volume seller = at least 100 complete single-seller orders
High-volume route = at least 200 complete single-seller orders

blocks.body:
### Where delay risk becomes visible
Purchase-to-carrier handoff is the only pre-delivery stage available in this source. Risk rises after four days and reaches 22.8% after seven days, versus 5.0% within two days. The largest seller exception was Seller 06A2C3; the largest route exception was SP to RJ. These are strong operational signals, not proof of fault.

### Three actions
1. Review Seller 06A2C3 and the next highest excess-volume sellers; trigger follow-up at four days without carrier handoff and escalation at seven.
2. Audit SP to RJ, RJ deliveries, and the Health Beauty category together to isolate route, assortment, and seller overlap.
3. Contact customers before a likely promise-date miss and apply service recovery to protect review scores.

### Limits
This is descriptive, not causal. The anonymized source covers Brazilian orders from 2016-2018 and does not include carrier scans, warehouse events, or last-mile checkpoints. Seller analysis excludes multi-seller orders to avoid assigning one delivery outcome to several sellers. Conflicting review scores are excluded from review comparisons.
